behavioral_effects: checks.process.check_coverage_floor_ratchet implements coverage-floor-does-not-regress: backend and governance-tool fail_under and the four vitest thresholds are compared with the base commit and any decrease is an issue unless a change record names the rule; registered as a fast check so pre-commit runs it too
check_policy_weakening_recorded compares against scope.since or HEAD instead of HEAD alone, so it can fire on a clean CI checkout

The CI governance job resolves a base commit (PR base sha, pre-push sha, or HEAD~1) and passes it as --since; it also runs make governance-sample and make governance-views and uploads the rendered views

New CI job governance-tool runs make governance-lint and make governance-selftest and uploads a third Codecov flag, governance; validators governance-lint and governance-sample added, governance-selftest re-pointed at the Make target

tools/repo_governance gains pytest-cov and ruff dev dependencies, a ratcheted coverage floor of 75, and an E501 ignore; 31 files reformatted, three real ruff findings fixed (a loop-variable closure in ts_imports, a nested if in renderers/context, an if/else in pipeline)
new_file_gate.py has 18 tests covering allow, ask, notebook_path, scratchpad, no-path and fail-open; test_coverage_ratchet.py has 11
compatibility_impact: governance-selftest's registered command is now make governance-selftest (pytest with coverage and --cov-config); it needs the tool's uv.lock, which now includes pytest-cov and ruff. check_policy_weakening_recorded and the new ratchet check compare against --since when CI passes it, HEAD otherwise, so their behaviour on a clean CI checkout changes from vacuous to real. E501 is ignored for the tool, mirroring the backend.
follow_up: Phase 3: hygiene job with pre-commit --all-files, actionlint and zizmor, hadolint, and range-scoped gitleaks
Watch the first CI run: the governance job now passes --since and the ratchet, change-record and policy-weakening checks evaluate the real commit range for the first time
limitations: Simplification pass: not run over the ruff reformat; the three hand edits are one-line rewrites
Phase 2 of the CI/CD coverage plan. Not here: hygiene job, docker matrix and GHCR publish, e2e, nightly, the ci.yml extractor that would let validators-declare-their-ci-job verify job names
reason: The governance tool that gates every other surface was itself never linted or coverage-measured (74 percent measured, no floor, no Codecov flag), the coverage-floor-does-not-regress rule had check_impl phase-5 and so was enforced by nobody, the change-record and policy-weakening checks were vacuous in CI because no --since range was passed, and new_file_gate.py had no test. After this change the governance-tool job runs ruff and pytest-cov with a ratcheted floor and uploads a governance flag, the ratchet check fails any lowered floor unless a change record names the rule, CI passes the real base commit to check --full, and every hook script has tests.
risks: The ratchet check is advisory by the maturity ladder; it reports, it does not fail CI. Promotion criteria are recorded in process.json
governance-views renders five pages per run; if a renderer starts needing --focus the target must be updated, and CI will say so
rollback: git revert. Nothing lives outside the repository except the governance flag on the Codecov instance, which simply stops receiving uploads.
security_impact: None. The governance-tool job runs with the workflow's contents: read permission and no backend install; the Codecov governance flag carries coverage data only. The ratchet check reads two pyproject files and one vitest config and never executes them.
summary: Lint and coverage-gate the governance tool, implement the coverage-floor ratchet check, and give CI the commit range its process checks need
